speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; let's start by asking when exactly these symptoms began and if you have any history of similar episodes or recent insect bites.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease (Lyme arthritis) with possible concurrent Disseminated Gonorrhea. The patient is a 17-year-old male from Minnesota presenting with a 3-day history of left wrist pain and fever, preceded by a self-resolving knee pain, which is highly suggestive of Lyme carditis or Lyme arthritis. The recent camping trip in Minnesota raises the suspicion of a tick bite and subsequent infection with Borrelia burgdorferi. The presence of sexually active partners also raises the possibility of disseminated gonorrhea causing septic arthritis. I will order tests to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology, Rheumatoid_Factor, ANA, CBC, CRP, ESR, Gonorrhea_NGCulture, WBC_Differential. REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray_left_wrist, Ultrasound_left_wrist.
